record_type_quote: Based on the (original) experiment by Chowdhury et al. (2017), we conducted laboratory experiments in several sessions in 2018 and 2022 at the OWL University of Applied Sciences and Arts in Lemgo, Germany in order to replicate their findings.

targets.authors: Chowdhury, S. M.; J. Y. Jeon; B. Saha
targets.title: Gender differences in the giving and taking variants of the dictator game.
targets.evidence_quote: We sought to replicate their study with German students at the OWL University of Applied Sciences and Arts using the same design as Chowdhury et al. (2017).
targets.outcome_quote: In general, our results do not provide support for significant differences between men and women in both the taking and the giving game, but additional analyses indicate that men are more likely than women to allocate nothing in the TG rather than in the GG. Thus, our results are partly consistent with Chowdhury et al.’s (2017) findings.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The concluding remarks explicitly give a partly-consistent verdict: general gender differences fail while selfish allocation patterns agree. The failed central linear effects alone do not override this stated aggregate partial agreement.
